prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Node.js project defines the lifecycle of its Long Term Support (LTS) releases through a structured schedule managed by the Release Working Group. According to the official documentation, an LTS release typically enters an "Active LTS" phase for 12 months, followed by a "Maintenance LTS" phase for 18 months, resulting in a total support duration of 30 months from the initial LTS start date.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-schedule | QUOTE: "Each major version of Node.js will be actively maintained for 12 months from the date it enters LTS coverage." | CLAIM: The Active LTS phase lasts for 12 months.
SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/release#release-schedule | QUOTE: "Following the 12 months of active maintenance, each major version will enter a period of maintenance for an additional 18 months." | CLAIM: The Maintenance LTS phase lasts for 18 months following the Active LTS phase.
